summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (writable primary), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys), using pg_basebackup with a dedicated replicator role. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys and standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory sequential node-restart protocol (standbys first, primary last) with boot-id proof of restart and post-restart recovery/data verification at each step.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/postgresql packages on node1, node2, node3 (AlmaLinux 9, PostgreSQL 13)
Initialized data directory on node1, configured listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Added pg_hba.conf entries permitting md5 replication connections from node2 and node3
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes (resolved 'No route to host' during pg_basebackup)
Generated a replication password on node1 and created a REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator'
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 on node2 and node3 to clone the primary and auto-generate standby.signal + primary_conninfo
Started PostgreSQL on node2 and node3, confirmed pg_is_in_recovery()=true and streaming state on primary
Created repl_test table on primary, inserted a row, verified it appeared on both standbys, and confirmed standbys reject INSERTs (read-only)
Captured baseline boot_id and health (postgresql active, replication/recovery status, row counts) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary) sequentially via systemctl reboot, polling until reachable and confirming changed boot_id after each
After each restart, verified postgresql active, correct recovery/primary role, data intact, and replication streaming state on remaining nodes
After primary restart, confirmed both standbys reconnected/streaming, then inserted a new row on the primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys
Deleted temporary password file from node1

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: Primary configured with replica wal_level and replicator role; standbys built via pg_basebackup -R with standby.signal/primary_conninfo present; pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both standbys; pg_stat_replication on primary shows both standbys 'streaming'

evidence.requirement: Changes on primary visible on both standbys (read-only enforcement)
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 primary; SELECT on node2 and node3 shows the row; INSERT attempted directly on each standby fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 97c5762b...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 6a7b0051... (changed); postgresql active, in recovery, data intact; primary shows node2 streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 15443601...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 8c4fede9... (changed); postgresql active, in recovery, data intact; primary shows both standbys streaming again

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state incl. cluster reconnection
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 989aa755...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id f68ee97d... (changed); postgresql active and pg_is_in_recovery()=false (primary role intact), pre-existing data present; both standbys reconnected as 'streaming'; new post-restart insert on primary replicated and verified present on node2 and node3
